evidence.quote: With greater confidence in achieving the inflation target, continued gradual increases in the federal funds rate are likely to be appropriate.
The most notable tailwind is the shift in America's fiscal policy stance from restraint to substantial stimulus in an economy close to full employment.
The persistence of subdued inflation, despite an unemployment rate that has moved below most estimates of its natural rate, suggests some risk that underlying inflation may have softened.
Historically, such episodes have tended to see elevated risks of imbalances, whether in the form of high inflation in earlier decades or of financial imbalances in recent decades.
Today, with headwinds shifting to tailwinds, the reverse could hold true.
balance sheet runoff is set to reach its steady-state pace later this year.

parsed.rationale: Brainard, previously dovish on low inflation, says strong tailwinds tip the balance toward continued gradual rate hikes and hints the path could be steeper, with attention to financial imbalances. Inflation is still characterized as subdued and a mild overshoot is tolerated, tempering the hawkish lean.
